For this analysis, I chose to use the xkcd color survey data. I am a fan of xkcd. 

TidyTuesday source: https://hardin47.github.io/TidyTuesday/2025-07-08/xkcd_color.html 

Data source: https://blog.xkcd.com/2010/05/03/color-survey-results/

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

The question I'm asking: Were more spam responses men or women? I'll be creating a histogram that looks to see what proportions of the responses with spam probability over 1 were men or women.  
```{r}
answers <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2025/2025-07-08/answers.csv')
color_ranks <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2025/2025-07-08/color_ranks.csv')
users <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2025/2025-07-08/users.csv')
#View(answers)
#View(color_ranks)
#View(users)

users |> arrange(y_chromosome) |> filter(y_chromosome >= 0) |> filter(spam_prob > 1) |> ggplot(
     aes(x = "", y = "", color = y_chromosome)) + 
    geom_col() + 
    labs (x = "spammer", y = "gender")

```    
As is expected, men are more likely to spam.
